title: Guarded decision matrix for safe application of batching & KV-cache recommendations
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem: Redwood Optimize will emit batching and KV-cache configuration recommendations that meaningfully change token throughput and per-token cost. Applying them automatically risks latency regressions, correctness changes, or customer-visible errors if done without staged validation.

Goal: Define and implement a guarded decision matrix and deployment choreography that lets Optimize recommendations be auto-applied safely for low-risk workloads while requiring operator review for high-risk cases. The system must support staged canaries, operator-in-the-loop approvals, automated rollback triggers, and observable metrics for fast triage.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Optimize recommendations can be classified into risk tiers via decision matrix (safe | moderate | high).
2) Safe-tier recommendations can be auto-applied with an automated staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with auto-rollback on policy violations.
3) Moderate-tier requires a single human approver in Console before stage rollout.
4) High-tier remains manual only and surfaces detailed simulation results.
5) Rollback actions can be executed automatically by the choreography engine within 60s of threshold violation or manually from Console.
6) End-to-end test coverage and a traffic-replay simulation harness validate the staging logic.
7) Documentation and runbook available for SRE and Solutions teams.
proposed_solution:
1) Decision Matrix: determine risk tier using heuristics: % expected cost reduction, predicted lat+regression delta (simulated), change to KV hit rate, model variant compatibility.
2) Choreography Engine: new lightweight orchestrator (stateless controller + persistent rollout state in control plane) that drives staged updates to runtime via the existing config API.
3) Canary Policy: cohort selection by customer-id hashing and region, with configurable initial percentage and escalation schedule.
4) Approval Workflow: Console surfaces 'Apply with Guardrails' flow; for moderate-tier require single approver; record approver, rationale, and link to simulation artifact.
5) Observability: wire p50/p95 latency, cost-per-token, generation error-rate, model output divergence score, and KV-hit-rate; expose per-cohort dashboards and alert rules.
6) Rollback: three rollback modes (immediate revert, gradual rollback, freeze and drain) selectable by policy.
7) Safety tests: traffic replay using representative traces and a 'shadow apply' mode to measure divergence before production rollout.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (ramp): land orchestration primitives and UI in staging; run shadow applies against 10 customers.
Phase 1 (pilot): enable on internal tenants + opt-in beta customers for safe-tier only (10% cohort).
Phase 2 (escalate): expand to 50% then 100% if thresholds pass.
Phase 3: enable moderate-tier with manual approval gate.
Phase 4: full telemetry-driven autopilot and runbook handoff.
canary_policy:
- Cohort hashing by account_id + region to ensure even distribution.
- Initial alpha size default 10% (configurable).
- Escalation: 10% -> 30% after 30m -> 100% after 3h if no alerts.
- Rollback triggers: p95 latency increase > 15% AND error-rate increase > 0.5% OR model divergence score > threshold.
- Canary dry-run: 'shadow apply' comparison window of 1h to compute divergence and cost delta.
observability_requirements:
- New rollout metrics: rollout_progress, cohort_size, applied_config_version.
- Per-cohort: latency_p50, latency_p95, error_rate, cost_per_request, kv_hit_rate, output_divergence_score.
- Alerts: auto rollback trigger and ops alert (PagerDuty) on sustained violations.
- Console: per-rollout timeline, ability to compare baseline vs current metrics, one-click rollback.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for decision matrix logic and policy evaluation.
2) Integration tests for orchestration controller applying configs to a local runtime mock.
3) E2E in staging using recorded traffic replays from production (anonymized) and shadow applies to compute divergence.
4) Chaos tests: simulate slow kernels / OOM on a subset of nodes to ensure rollback works and does not escalate blast radius.
5) Safety runbook drills with SRE team and Solutions Engineering to test human approval flows.
comments: 2025-03-12 Aisha Park: Created ticket. Initial draft of matrix and choreography. Blocking: orchestration primitives and rollout metrics need product review.
2025-03-14 Miguel Torres: POC of decision matrix implemented in /dev. Early heuristic: cost reduction > 5% and predicted latency delta < 5% -> safe. Need to tune thresholds after simulation runs.
2025-03-16 Design review (Anika Rao): Console flow draft uploaded to Drive and linked. Suggested showing expected cost delta prominently and requiring a rationale field for manual approvals.
2025-03-18 SRE sync (Liam Chen): Agreed on rollback SLAs (controller must initiate revert within 60s of threshold). Will provide PagerDuty escalation policy. Added chaos test to staging pipeline.

2025-03-20 Miguel Torres: Implemented shadow-apply mode and produced first divergence report for three representative workloads. One workload showed model-output divergence above threshold in certain long-sequence cases; flagged as moderate-tier. Next: refine cohort selection and extend simulation traces.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: more aggressive auto-apply reduces cost faster but increases risk of subtle quality regressions; decision matrix balances economic benefit vs predicted risk. We are starting conservative (safe-tier only) and will iterate thresholds with richer simulation data.
